findings.claim: The architecture overview's row for kmctl plugin patch said --undo deletes the plugin folder and the OpenCode files with no scope.
The r3 test checked only for "With `--scope user`" and the word "leaves", which would pass if the new sentence changed.

verdict.text: Both findings sent back are fixed and nothing they touched broke.
The gates are green on this tree.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format, tests, integration and eval rows r1 to r4 all pass.
I read the diff of `.okf/architecture/overview.md`, `docs/reference/commands.md` and the r3 test in `tests/test_plugin_patch.py`.
The rewrapped reference sentence keeps the same words, sits on its own lines, and the test joins whitespace before matching, so the wrap cannot break it.
The overview row now ends "and with `--scope user` deletes nothing in the repository and names them", which matches what `unpatch` does.

`test_undo_docs_say_user_scope_leaves_project_files` now checks the full new help sentence ("... which are patched at project scope only, and names them") and the new reference sentence ("deletes nothing in this repository: it leaves `.agents/plugins/kmctl/` and the OpenCode files") word for word.
Neither phrase appears elsewhere, so the test fails if either sentence is dropped or changed.
